title: Finite Weil divisors and effective Q-Cartier Weil divisors on schemes
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Define the set of codimension-one points to be $X^{(1)}=\{x\in X:\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=1\}$, where dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. A finite Weil divisor is a finitely supported integer function $E:X^{(1)}\to\mathbf Z$, with support $\bigcup_{E(x)\ne0}\overline{\{x\}}$. On a normal Noetherian scheme these are exactly finite integral combinations of the integral codimension-one reduced closed subschemes. For an effective Cartier ideal $C$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], say that $C$ has effective Weil divisor $E$ if every point admits an affine neighbourhood $U$ with $C|_U=(c)$ for a non-zero-divisor $c\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, and for every $x\in X^{(1)}\cap U$ the coefficient $E(x)$ equals the finite length [def-weil-pbc-module-length] of $\mathcal O_{X,x}/(c_x)$. (On normal Noetherian schemes the local ring is a DVR, so this length is the normalized vanishing order.) An effective Q-Cartier Weil divisor is such a finite divisor with $E(x)\ge0$ for all $x$, for which there exist a single positive integer $n$ and an effective Cartier ideal with effective Weil divisor $nE$.
